Figure 1a. Top half of architecture diagram. Continuation marker at bottom.

Top half of a service architecture flow diagram displayed on a grid background. The diagram contains four rows of connected service nodes, each row consisting of three rounded-rectangle boxes connected left-to-right by arrows. Row 1 (top): 'Service 1 / ID SVC-100' (light blue) → 'Service 2 / ID SVC-101' (light green) → 'Service 3 / ID SVC-102' (light orange/peach). Row 2: 'Service 4 / ID SVC-103' (light purple/lavender) → 'Service 5 / ID SVC-104' (light blue) → 'Service 6 / ID SVC-105' (light green). Row 3: 'Service 7 / ID SVC-106' (light orange/peach) → 'Service 8 / ID SVC-107' (light purple/lavender) → 'Service 9 / ID SVC-108' (light blue). Row 4 (partially visible at bottom, cut by page boundary): 'Service 10 / ID SVC-109' (light green) → 'Service 11 / ID SVC-110' (light orange/peach) → 'Service 12 / ID SVC-111' (light purple/lavender). Diagonal black lines connect the end of each row to the beginning of the next row below. A thick horizontal red line marks the page boundary across the bottom of the diagram. A red text label reads: 'IMPORTANT: THIS FIGURE CONTINUES ON NEXT PAGE - boundary line must reconcile'.
